Modified read with Beige Book context:

- Policy decision: Clear dovish pivot. The FOMC cut the target range 50 bp to 4.75–5.00%, cited “greater confidence” inflation is moving sustainably toward 2%, and said risks to employment and inflation are “roughly in balance.” Quantitative tightening caps remain unchanged; administered rates reset (IORB 4.9%, ON RRP 4.8%). One dissent (Bowman) favored a 25 bp cut. Primary credit rate lowered to 5.0%.

- Beige Book (Aug 26, 2024) overlay: District reports point to modest overall activity, cooler labor markets, and easing wage pressures, with consumer spending mixed/soft in several areas. Price increases continued to moderate but remained above pre-pandemic norms. CRE stress—especially office and some construction—persisted, and credit conditions stayed tight. These findings align with SLOOS: banks continue to tighten standards across C&I, CRE, and consumer credit; loan demand remains weak; and delinquencies in some consumer categories are edging higher. Forward-looking commentary indicates banks plan to keep standards tight through late 2024 amid collateral and macro uncertainty.

- Implications: The sizable rate cut and “balanced risks” language should support near-term financial conditions, but Beige Book and SLOOS suggest bank-intermediated credit will remain constrained, muting the transmission of easier policy. Combined with a cooling labor market and moderating inflation, the outlook is cautiously constructive rather than outright risk-on.

Net tone: Positive but restrained given ongoing tight lending, soft loan demand, and CRE headwinds, even as inflation progress and the policy pivot reduce downside inflation risk.
